gridNotes.nasal|pharyngeal: A nasal needs an oral closure above a lowered velum. There is nothing above the pharynx to close.
gridNotes.nasal|glottal: The glottis sits below the velum, so air can never be routed through the nose from there.
gridNotes.trill|palatal: The tongue body is too massive to sustain aerodynamic flutter against the hard palate.
gridNotes.trill|velar: Same mass problem: the tongue body will not oscillate freely at the velum.
gridNotes.trill|glottal: Vocal folds vibrate, but that is phonation, not a trill of a supraglottal articulator.
gridNotes.lateral|bilabial: Lips have no side channel — there is no 'around' for the air to pass.
gridNotes.lateral|labiodental: Same as bilabial: no lateral channel exists at the lips.
gridNotes.lateral|uvular: Behind the velum the airway is a single tube with no sides to flow around.
gridNotes.lateral|pharyngeal: No lateral channel exists in the pharynx.
gridNotes.lateral|glottal: No lateral channel exists at the glottis.
gridNotes.click|labiodental: A click needs a sealed pocket between two closures; teeth and lip cannot form the front seal.
gridNotes.click|velar: The velum is already the back closure of every click, so it cannot also be the front one.
gridNotes.click|uvular: Behind the velar back closure there is no cavity left to rarefy.
gridNotes.click|pharyngeal: Too far back — the rarefiable pocket lies in front of the velum.
gridNotes.click|glottal: Too far back, and the glottis cannot seal a lingual cavity.
gridNotes.ejective|glottal: An ejective is powered by a raised closed glottis. The glottis cannot be both the piston and the valve.
gridNotes.implosive|pharyngeal: Implosives need a lowering larynx below an oral closure; the pharynx is not above the larynx.
gridNotes.implosive|glottal: Same conflict as the glottal ejective — one glottis cannot do both jobs.
gridNotes.whistle|glottal: Whistling needs a resonating cavity in front of a narrow jet. The glottis has neither.
gridNotes.phonation|bilabial: Phonation is what the larynx does. No other articulator has folds to vibrate.
gridNotes.phonation|alveolar: Phonation is what the larynx does. No other articulator has folds to vibrate.
gridNotes.phonation|velar: Phonation is what the larynx does. No other articulator has folds to vibrate.
gridNotes.percussive|labiodental: Nothing can strike here without also closing the airway.
gridNotes.percussive|postalveolar: Struck sounds need two hard surfaces meeting; the tongue behind the ridge is soft tissue against soft tissue.
gridNotes.percussive|palatal: No two hard surfaces meet here.
gridNotes.percussive|velar: No two hard surfaces meet here.
gridNotes.percussive|uvular: The uvula is soft tissue; it slaps but does not strike percussively.
